newsitem.title: USA: N.J. gives $25 mln more for school debt service.
newsitem.headline: N.J. gives $25 mln more for school debt service.

text.p: New Jersey's $16.8 billion fiscal 1998 budget package includes an extra $25 million in debt service aid to local school districts.
Gov. Christine Whitman said the aid would help pay off capital construction projects and help lower property taxes.

"Now with this additional $25 million in debt service aid, added to the $70 million originally proposed in the budget, we will be providing the schools with a total of $95 million in debt service aid -- easing the burden on local taxpayers," Whitman said in a statement.
Whitman's Democratic opponents have blamed her fiscal policies for rising property taxes in the state.

More than 300 school districts will be eligible for the aid, which must be used to lower debt service tax levies. The legislature is expected to vote on the budget next week, but little opposition is expected.
